facts: SNPs (Single Nucleotide Polymorphisms) are the most common type of genetic variation.
If uncoiled, the DNA in all your cells would reach the sun and back multiple times.
The HERC2 gene is a key switch that determines blue or brown eye color.
DNA Phenotyping uses genetics to predict physical appearance like hair and skin color.
CRISPR-Cas9 is a revolutionary tool used to 'edit' specific parts of the genome.
Genes are small segments of DNA that carry instructions for making proteins.
Humans share about 60% of their DNA with bananas.
Your genome contains about 20,000 to 25,000 distinct genes.
The MC1R gene is primarily responsible for red hair and fair skin.
DNA is shaped like a twisted ladder, known as a Double Helix.
Most of our DNA (about 98%) is 'non-coding,' previously called 'junk DNA.'
Mitochondrial DNA is inherited exclusively from your mother.
Environmental factors can change how your genes work; this is called Epigenetics.
The SLC24A5 gene plays a major role in determining human skin pigmentation.
DNA is found in the nucleus of the cell, but some is also in mitochondria.
A 'Codon' is a sequence of three DNA bases that codes for a specific amino acid.
Your DNA can be damaged by UV light, chemicals, and even normal cellular processes.
The Four Letters: DNA uses only four chemical bases: Adenine (A), Guanine (G), Cytosine (C), and Thymine (T).
SNP Frequency: SNPs occur once every 300 nucleotides on average.
Health Markers: SNPs can help predict a person’s response to certain drugs or susceptibility to diseases.
Evolutionary Traces: SNPs act as biological markers, helping scientists track how humans migrated over history.
Genotype vs. Phenotype: Genotype is your genetic makeup; Phenotype is how those genes actually look.
Mutation vs. Variation: A mutation is rare, while a SNP is a common variation found in at least 1% of the population.
DNA Sequencing: This is the process of determining the exact order of the 3 billion bases in our genome.
The Eye Color Myth: Eye color isn't determined by one gene; it is a complex trait involving multiple SNPs.
Biogeographical Ancestry: DNA can pinpoint where your ancestors came from with incredible geographic precision.
Age Estimation: Advanced DNA analysis can even estimate a person’s age within a few years.
Melanin Genes: Specific genes like MC1R determine whether you will have red hair or freckles.
Self-Repair: Your cells have specialized proteins that constantly scan and repair damaged DNA.
Telomeres & Aging: Telomeres are protective caps at the ends of DNA strands that act like a biological clock.
SNP Profiles: Law enforcement uses SNPs to create a unique DNA Fingerprint different for every person.
The 'Cleft Chin' Gene: Having a dimple in your chin is a dominant genetic trait caused by bone structure.
Photic Sneeze Reflex: Some people sneeze when looking at the sun; this is called ACHOO syndrome.
Biological Age: DNA methylation patterns can tell you your True Biological Age.
Micro-chimerism: During pregnancy, some of the baby's DNA can stay in the mother's body for decades.
